# Carola (02, engineer) — BAD-015

## Brief
Objective: make both export end cards print `my.badtakes.io/@handle` when the signed-in account has a handle, and `badtakes.io` exactly as today when it does not, when the switch is off, or when the draw fails. An export never fails for the sake of a watermark.

The design is already made: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-20-user-profiles-and-handles-design.md, section "The handle on exports" (read the whole spec once, then that section closely). Build exactly that:
 - Vertical reel (renderer/reel.js): the `badtakes.io` line becomes the profile URL, drawn with the existing pinnedText helper so a variable-length string never overflows the card; brand artwork stays programmatic, never loaded as images (canvas taint).
 - Landscape .mp4: `src/brand.js` changes by nothing and `test/brand.test.js` is not modified. brandedExportArgs takes endCard as a file path (main.js around line 2856 uses brand/endcard-1080p.png). The renderer draws the whole card to a PNG and hands it through the export IPC; main writes it to temp and passes that path instead of the static asset; the same shape as reel:frames (renderer draws, main writes, ffmpeg reads a path). On any failure the static brand/endcard-1080p.png is used, exactly as today.
 - Both cards draw the URL line from one shared routine so they cannot drift. Put that routine in src/ (plain Node, no Electron imports, taking a 2d context or returning layout numbers) so it is unit-testable; the renderer has no test harness.
 - A Settings toggle `handleOnExports`, default on, controls both cards (renderer/CLAUDE.md for the Settings vocabulary; the settings store in main.js).
 - Offline: the handle comes from the cached licence status (licenseStatus / license.json), so an export with no network is still attributed.
 - The render service: the web app exports through the container (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-web-render-service-design.md, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-11-reel-in-the-container.md, scripts/web-api.js around line 472 which uses the static endcard, container/reel.js, container/credit.js, container/check-image.js). Make the container path honour the handle the same way when the request carries one, and never fail an export when it does not. Read how the web app already knows its handle (web/account.js:338) and how the export request reaches scripts/web-api.js before deciding the wire shape.
 - src/handles.js profileUrl and server/supabase/functions/_shared/handles.mjs profileUrl are the two copies of the URL rule; use them, never a third string. Do not touch mobile/ios/App/App/public (a build output).

Verification (the tiers in .claude/skills/implementing-changes/SKILL.md; quote output, never "it should work"):
 - `npm test`, and say whether the pack tests ran or skipped (this worktree has voicepacks linked, so they should run).
 - A full `npm run smoke` (the reel leg is last and needs the screening's auto-save): `BT_LIBRARY_ROOT=/tmp/bt-lib-bad-015-public-profiles SMOKE_DIR=/tmp/smoke-bad-015-public-profiles npm run smoke`, SMOKE_OK printed and exit 0; open the reel screenshot. The smoke run has no handle, so it proves the no-handle path. For the handle path, add an unpackaged-only override the way BT_LICENSE_BYPASS works (for example BT_HANDLE=eric alongside the bypass; main.js and src/license-config.js; unpackaged only, like every other bypass) and run the smoke again with it, then inspect the reel end-card screenshot and the exported .mp4's last second (ffmpeg -ss near the end, one frame to PNG) to show the URL. The fake camera encodes 0-byte VP8, so judge the reel by files and state, not by webcam frames.
 - test/reelrender.integration.test.js covers the container reel; run it and whatever container tests cover the credit and end card.
 - `test/brand.test.js` unchanged is the evidence that src/brand.js changed by nothing; say so.
Before starting: this worktree is wired (scripts/worktree-init.sh ran: voicepacks linked, smoke library at /tmp/bt-lib-bad-015-public-profiles). Never run npm install here. Use the superpowers test-driven-development skill for the src/ routine and the IPC contract.
